title: Patient Payment Plans Installment Agreement Terms: Due Day, First Due Date and Reminders
content:
Under every Patient Payment Plans installment agreement the patient's installments fall due on a chosen day of the month. The terms below fix, for each tier, the latest day that may be chosen, the spacing between signing and the first installment, and the lead time of the reminder that precedes each due date.

### Terms by tier

| Tier | Latest due day that may be chosen (earliest is day 1) | Calendar days after signing that set the first due date | Days before each due date that the reminder or pre-debit notice is sent |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3-Month Interest-Free Plan | 28 | 30 | 5 |
| 6-Month Interest-Free Plan | 28 | 30 | 5 |
| 12-Month Interest-Free Plan | 28 | 30 | 5 |
| 18-Month Extended Plan | 28 | 30 | 5 |
| 24-Month Extended Plan | 28 | 30 | 5 |
| Financial Hardship Plan | 28 | 45 | 5 |

### Conditions

1. The due day may be any day from day 1 to day 28 of the month on every tier.
2. The first due date is the first chosen due day on or after the signing date plus the tier's number of calendar days in the table: 30 days on the five tiers other than the Financial Hardship Plan, and 45 days on the Financial Hardship Plan.
3. A reminder, or with automatic debit a pre-debit notice, is sent 5 days before each due date on every tier.

### Illustration (hypothetical dates)

On a hypothetical 6-Month Interest-Free Plan signed on 3 March with the 10th chosen as due day, the date 30 calendar days after signing is 2 April; the first 10th on or after that date is 10 April, which is the first due date. Under a Financial Hardship Plan signed the same day with the same due day, the date 45 calendar days after signing is 17 April, and the first due date is 10 May. With a first due date of 10 April, the reminder is sent on 5 April.
